paper.title: Active Ranking of Experts Based on their Performances in Many Tasks

unmapped: Arms are expert-task pairs (i,j) of an n x d mean matrix M; the learner queries one entry per round
Monotonicity: rows of M are totally ordered entrywise up to an unknown permutation (expert i better than k on every task)
Goal is identifying the better expert (row), not the best entry
Identifiability: the two expert rows differ on at least one task
settings.definition_quote: We consider that the performance of each expert $i \in \intr{n}$ on task $j \in \intr{d}$ is modeled via random variable following an unknown $1$-sub-Gaussain distribution $\nu_{ij}$ with mean $M_{ij}$ ... Monotonicity: there exists a permutation $\pi$ such that $M_{\pi(i)j} \ge M_{\pi(i+1)j}$.

unmapped: Arms are expert-task pairs (i,j) of an n x d mean matrix M; the learner queries one entry per round
Monotonicity: rows of M totally ordered entrywise up to unknown permutation
Goal: recover the full ranking of the n experts with probability >= 1-delta (fixed confidence)
Identifiability: all expert rows pairwise distinct
settings.definition_quote: Ranking identification (R): the learner aims at outputting a ranking $\hat{\pi}$ that estimates $\pi$. For a given confidence parameter $\delta \in (0,1)$, we say that it is $\delta$-accurate for ranking if it satisfies: $\mathbb{P}( \hat{\pi} \neq \pi) \le \delta$

unmapped: Arms are expert-task pairs (i,j) of an n x d mean matrix M; the learner queries one entry per round
Monotonicity: rows of M totally ordered entrywise up to unknown permutation
Goal: identify the best expert (row) rather than best entry
Identifiability: the best expert row differs from every other row
settings.definition_quote: Best-expert identification (B): the learner aims at outputting an expert $\hat{k}$ that estimates the best performing expert, namely $\pi(1)$. ... $\mathbb{P}( \hat{k} \neq \pi(1)) \le \delta$.

source.label: thm:up2
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assump} holds. For $\delta \in (0,1)$, $\epsilon > 0$, consider Algorithm~\ref{algo1} with input $(\delta, \epsilon)$. Define $H := \frac{d}{\norm{M_1 - M_2}_2^2}$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, we have ... output $\hat{k} \in \{null, \pi(1)\}$; If $\epsilon < \norm{M_1 - M_2}_2$, ... $\hat{k} = \pi(1)$. Moreover, with probability at least $1-\delta$, its total number of queries ... $N \le \tilde c \times \log(1/\delta)H_{\epsilon}$

results.notes: Statement mentions a numerical constant c not shown in tilde c; recorded as O. Also guarantees correctness (output in {null, pi(1)}, and pi(1) when epsilon < ||M1-M2||). With epsilon=0, H_eps = H.

source.label: thm:upn
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assump} holds. Let $\delta \in (0,1)$, and define for $i \in \intr{n-1}$: $H_i := \frac{d}{\norm{M_{\pi(i)} - M_{\pi(i+1)}}_2^2}$. Let $H^* = \max_{i \le n-1} H_i$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{algo4} outputs the correct ranking, and its total number of queries (denoted $N$) is upper bounded by: $N \le \tilde{c} \times \log(1/\delta) \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} H_i$, where $\tilde{c} = c\log(n)\log^2(d)\log(H^*)\log(n\log(H^*\vee d))$

source.label: thm:be
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assump} holds. Let $\delta \in (0,1)$, and define for $i \in \intr{2,n}$: $G_i := \frac{d}{\norm{M_{\pi(1)} - M_{\pi(i)}}_2^2}$. Let $G^* = \max_{i} G_i$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{algo7} outputs $\pi(1)$, and the total number of queries satisfies $N \le \tilde{c} \times \log(1/\delta) \sum_{i=2}^{n} G_i$, with $\tilde{c} = c\log^{2}(d)\log^2\left(G^*\right) \log(n\log(d))$

symbols.D_sq: ||(M_0)_1 - (M_0)_2||_2^2, squared L2 distance between the two experts

conditions: any delta-accurate algorithm for ranking / best expert identification
worst case over the class D_{M_0} of 1-sub-Gaussian problems whose gap vector is a permutation of that of M_0
the event N >= bound holds with probability at least delta for some instance in the class

source.label: thm:lwrn
source.quote: Fix $n=2$. Let $d\geq 1$ and $\delta\in (0,1/4)$. Consider any matrix $M_0\in \mathcal{M}_{2,d}$. For any $\delta$-accurate algorithm $A$ ..., we have: $\max_{\cB \in \mathbb{D}_{M_0}} \mathbb{P}_{\cB, A}\left[N \ge \frac{d}{2\|(M_0)_{1,.}-(M_0)_{2,.}\|_2^2} \log\left(\frac{1}{6\delta}\right)\right]\geq \delta$

results.notes: Probability of the lower-bound event is at least delta (not 1-delta), recorded as high_probability for lack of better vocabulary.

symbols.sum_inv_Dsq: sum_{i=1}^{n-1} 1/Delta_i^2 where Delta_i = ||M_{pi(i)} - M_{pi(i+1)}||_2 (fixed L2 distances between consecutive experts)

conditions: any delta-accurate algorithm for ranking identification
worst case over the class D_Delta^{n,d} of 1-sub-Gaussian problems with fixed consecutive L2 distances

source.label: thm:lwrn_minimax
source.quote: Let $n, d \ge 1$, $\delta \in (0,1)$. For any $\delta$-accurate algorithm $A$ for ranking identification $\bm{(R)}$, we have: $\max_{\cB \in \mathbb{D}^{n,d}_{\bm{\Delta}}} \mathbb{E}_{\cB, A}[N] \ge \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{d}{\Delta_i^2} \log(1/(4\delta))$.

results.notes: Proof uses constant-row instances reducing to two-arm BAI (Kaufmann et al. 2016).

conditions: any delta-accurate algorithm for best expert identification
worst case over the class bar D^{n,d} of 1-sub-Gaussian problems with ||M_{pi(1)} - M_{pi(i+1)}||_2^2 >= bar_Delta_i^2

source.label: thm:lwrn_minimax_best_arm
source.quote: Let $n, d \ge 1$, $\delta \in (0,1)$. For any $\delta$-accurate algorithm $A$ for best expert identification $\bm{(B)}$, we have: $\min_{A \in \bA(\delta)} \max_{\cB \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}^{n,d}_{\bm{\Delta}}} \mathbb{E}_{\cB, A}[N] \ge \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}\frac{d}{\overline{\Delta}_i^2} \log(1/(4\delta))$

results.notes: Proof: straightforward consequence of standard BAI lower bounds on constant-row instances.
